title: Premium iOS Keyboard Themes
designIntent: Vier eigenständige Oberflächen auf einer vertrauten, systemnahen iPhone-Tastatur. Theme-Wechsel ändern Farben und Oberflächen, niemals die Tastenlogik oder das Layout.

references.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines - Dark Mode
Community discussion - theme readability and customization (anecdotal feedback)
Community discussion - iPhone keyboard layout and usability (anecdotal feedback)

implementationPrinciples: Keep the existing keyboard model, input handling, row layout, prediction bar, shift/delete behavior, return-key logic, accessibility identifiers, and extension lifecycle intact.
Use the current project's geometry as the source of truth. Do not hard-code a single iPhone width or fixed total keyboard height.
Use colors consistently by semantic role. Accent colors are primarily for theme selection and small interactive indicators, not every key.
For small keyboard labels, target at least 4.5:1 contrast and test with Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency.
Slate Glass must remain readable if system transparency is reduced or material rendering is unavailable; provide an opaque fallback.
No neon, rainbow gradients, heavy shadows, fake 3D keycaps, ornamental labels, or oversized animations.

geometry.layoutReference: Follow the familiar Apple iOS keyboard hierarchy and the project's existing key placement exactly.

horizontalInsetPt.note: Use existing value if already tuned.

geometry.keyLabelFont: Use the project's existing system font sizing. If rebuilding, start with a system font around 19-21 pt for letter keys and validate on compact/large iPhones.
rows: Prediction/suggestion strip only if already supported by the project.
QWERTZ row including German characters according to the active language layout.
Bottom row preserves existing 123/globe-or-emoji/space/return/microphone controls and widths.

shared.symbolStyle: SF Symbols or the project's existing system-style vector icons; do not replace controls with emoji.
shared.specialKeyRule: Special keys are distinct through a restrained tone difference, not bright colored fills.
shared.pressedStateRule: Use a subtle role-specific fill shift or a dark/white overlay; keep labels stable and legible.
shared.selectionStateRule: Show theme selection in the Theme Studio UI, not as persistent decorative marks on live keyboard keys.

cupertino-native.intent: The closest match to Apple's familiar keyboard. System-adaptive light and dark appearances, understated separation, no custom decorative effect.

geometryOverrides.shadow: none or the existing native-style shadow only

notes: Prefer semantic UIKit/SwiftUI system colors in production when they match the design; listed HEX values are design targets for previews and regression tests.

nord-minimal.intent: Distinctive cool blue-gray palette, quiet but not flat, with a restrained icy-cyan accent used sparingly.
notes: Nord remains intentionally dark in both OS appearances; do not automatically remap it to a light palette.
Use the cyan only for selection/accent details, not for all letter labels.

slate-glass.intent: A premium, controlled glass look: translucent key surfaces, subtle edge highlights, charcoal base. No bright blur glow.

geometryOverrides.shadow: none; let a fine border and material do the work

notes: HEX alpha suffixes are 8-digit RGBA-style web notation: #RRGGBBAA. Convert carefully if your parser expects #AARRGGBB.
Apply a SwiftUI Material in the rendering layer, then a restrained translucent tint. Color opacity alone is not blur.
If Reduce Transparency is enabled or the extension cannot provide reliable material context, switch to an opaque #343B47-like key surface while preserving text contrast.
Do not blur or obscure the glyphs; the glass effect should be visible mainly in surface edges and soft tonal separation.

midnight-oled.intent: True black keyboard surface, graphite keycaps, fine borders and near-white typography. Quiet premium contrast.
notes: True black applies to the keyboard background only; individual keycaps must remain visibly separated.
Avoid pure-white text on every secondary label; reserve #F2F2F7 for primary glyphs.
Treat OLED power savings as a potential benefit of black pixels, not as a guaranteed percentage claim.
